finding: The DRAFT row — the only entrance to agent mode — carries two board destinations that disagree with each other and with the product: the button itself goes to 170:29 (thinking) while an overlaying hotspot on the same board goes to 170:41 (planning), and in code it starts nothing at all.

finding: The plan-approval gate the board draws does not exist in the product: the runner goes from plan-received to running step 1 in the same breath, so there is no state in which a plan is listed and waiting, and neither "Edit plan" nor "Run 3 steps" has anywhere to live.

finding: ⌘K is bound twice with no guard between them — the shell palette and the Pages panel's jump-to-page palette each attach their own unconditional keydown listener — so with Pages open one press reaches both, and no board in this section records that a second ⌘K palette exists.
evidence: StudioHeader.tsx:249-266 document.addEventListener("keydown") → setCmdOpen(v=>!v); PagesTab.tsx:125-136 window.addEventListener("keydown") → setPaletteOpen(open=>!open). PagesTab calls e.preventDefault() but not stopPropagation, and both handlers are bubble-phase, so both run. The Pages palette is board 1171:4807 (Pages section), documented in PageCommandPalette.tsx:1-14. NOT VERIFIED LIVE — this is a static reading of the two listeners.
fix: Decide the ownership (suggest: PagesTab only binds while the panel has focus, or drops ⌘K in favour of a panel-local chord), then record the outcome on 1779:3 — it is the section that already flags "one decision open".

finding: The board that defines the disabled-row treatment does it with two reasons the palette cannot produce: "needs approval" and "admin only" are permission states, and the palette's guard only knows about selection and history — neither Publish nor Rollback is a palette command at all.

CommandPalette.tsx:175-195 registryGuard returns only "select two or more", "select a group", "nothing copied", "nothing selected"; the hardcoded rows add "nothing to undo"/"nothing to redo" (lines 76, 85). No `publish` or `rollback` command exists in engine/commands/defaultCommands.ts; Publish is a rail TAB (tabsConfig.ts:206, shortcut "U" at :210), so the palette can only ever offer "Open Publish panel".
fix: Either add a role/approval guard that produces those two reasons for real Publish/Rollback commands, or redraw 166:58 with reasons the palette emits ("nothing selected", "nothing to undo"). Caption 172:22's argument is right; the example under it is not buildable.

finding: The one state where the run is parked and a user is most likely to want out is the only run board that drops Stop — and caption 172:37 promises "Stop is always reachable". The code does render it there.

finding: The step-glyph vocabulary the caption fixes is not the one the code emits: skipped is ⊘ on the boards and "–" in code, a step waiting on the user reuses the running dot so the two are indistinguishable, and the "no change" outcome has no glyph of its own on any board.

AgentPlan.tsx:67-75 STEP_GLYPH = {pending:"○", running:"●", awaiting:"●", applied:"✓", skipped:"–", nochange:"–", failed:"✕"}; useAgentRunner.ts:194 produces the `nochange` status the boards never show.
fix: Settle one table: give `skipped` ⊘, give `awaiting` its own glyph (the gate is a pause, not a run), and draw a `nochange` row on 170:70 or 171:67.

finding: The recovery job has no board. When the model provider itself fails, the panel shows a third error state — "The AI service didn't respond." with the server's line and a Try again that re-runs the last prompt — and the code's own comment says the boards do not draw it. It is also the state a user hits after a silent reconnect loop, so it is the one they most need explained.
evidence: AITab.tsx:299-329 renders it, with the comment at :300-304 "The third state the boards do not draw…"; useStreamPrompt.ts:134-159 produces errorKind "other" from both onError and the reconnect-budget path. Section 1776:8380 has exactly two error boards, 171:105 (quota) and 171:136 (not-configured).
fix: Build "AI · error-provider" from 171:105: same block shape on --bk-error-tint, title "The AI service didn't respond.", body "Nothing was changed…", the server's own line beneath, and a "Try again" link. Wire 170:29 → it, and it → 170:29.

finding: Applying a chat diff has three outcomes and none is boarded — most importantly "Nothing to apply — no change this editor can make", which is what a user gets when the model answers with a command batch this editor cannot map. That case used to read "✓ Applied" over an unchanged page, so it is the outcome that exists because it was got wrong.
evidence: ChatMessage.tsx:52-63 renders "✓ Applied" / "Nothing to apply — no change this editor can make" / "Discarded" from edit.state; AITab.tsx:183-192 sets outcome = applied>0 || proposals.length>0 ? "applied" : "invalid"; types.ts:21 state: "pending"|"applied"|"rejected"|"invalid".
fix: Draw the three resolved states of the proposal card as variants of the new chat proposal board (W-K-01), replacing its Discard/Apply row with the resolved line.

finding: A multi-selection has a scope band and a refusal in code, and neither is drawn — while a button labelled "Ask AI about this selection" sits on the multi-select toolbar and opens this panel. finding: The canvas palette is a one-board family: it has no typing, no-results or empty state, and its dead end is a bare "No commands found" with none of the AI hand-off the shell palette gets six boards to explain.
